claims.text: The starting catalyst is a multi-element automotive alloy containing several principal elements in nearly equiatomic ratios.
The starting catalyst has low platinum-group-metal content.
A nanometer-scale, uniform CeO2 layer can be deposited onto the catalyst surface.
The deposited CeO2 layer functions as an oxygen-storage material.
The CeO2 layer forms a stable interface with the underlying multi-element alloy.
The CeO2 layer facilitates dynamic oxygen storage and release at active sites.
Dynamic oxygen storage and release helps regenerate oxygen-deficient regions of the catalyst.
The CeO2 layer protects the catalyst against sintering.
The CeO2 layer protects the catalyst against poisoning during exposure to exhaust constituents including H2O and NO.
The proposed CeO2 treatment preserves catalytic activity and durability without increasing platinum usage.
Relative to an untreated catalyst, the CeO2-coated catalyst will retain more catalytic activity during prolonged simulated exhaust exposure.
Relative to an untreated catalyst, the CeO2-coated catalyst will have improved durability during prolonged simulated exhaust exposure.
The predicted improvements apply under transient, low-temperature automotive exhaust conditions involving H2O, NO, and thermal aging.
